docs.title: pointclouds
docs.text:
Read, filter, decimate and grid point clouds (LAS / LAZ / COPC) in Python, with an optional bridge to the pyramids GIS engine.

See Installation to get started.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Reading is header-first: opening a file reads its header and nothing else, so metadata costs the same whether the file holds four hundred points or four billion. The record arrays decompress the moment you touch one.

import pointclouds as pc

cloud = pc.PointCloud.read_file("examples/data/sample.laz")

cloud.crs         # CRS.from_epsg(28992) - from the header
cloud.bounds      # (155000.0, 463000.0, 155038.0, 463038.0)
cloud.count       # 400, straight from the header: no record was read
cloud.dimensions  # ('X', 'Y', 'Z', 'intensity', 'return_number', ...)

xyz = cloud.to_array(("X", "Y", "Z"))   # (400, 3) - this is what loads the records

Two things worth knowing:

  • cloud.count is the header's point count and is free. len(cloud) is how many points are in memory, so on a freshly opened cloud it triggers the read. They agree once the records are loaded.
  • Pass lazy=False to read_file to read the records up front, and cloud.loaded tells you which state you are in without changing it.

Everything above runs on the bare install — numpy, laspy, pyproj and scipy, with no GDAL anywhere. The pyramids converters are a separate, optional step behind the [gis] extra.

docs.title: Sample data
docs.text: examples/data/sample.las and sample.laz are small synthetic fixtures (400 points on a 20 × 20 grid in EPSG:28992, with ground and vegetation classes). They are committed, so nothing needs downloading; examples/data/make_sample.py regenerates them.

docs.title: Development environment
docs.text:
The repo is managed with pixi; pixi.lock is committed and CI installs from it. Everything below assumes pixi 0.73 or newer — that is the version pinned in the workflows, and the lock is format v7, which older pixi refuses to read.

Before the first pixi install, decide where the environments go. The manifest declares nine of them, and a full set is several GB. By default pixi materialises them in .pixi/envs/ inside the checkout, which is the wrong place if your clone lives in a synced folder (OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive): the sync client locks files mid-install and you get permission errors on the next install or clean. Point pixi somewhere outside the tree instead:

pixi config set --local detached-environments "C:/python-environments/pixi/envs"   # Windows
pixi config set --local detached-environments "$HOME/.cache/pixi/envs"            # Linux / macOS

That writes .pixi/config.toml, which is deliberately not tracked — it holds an absolute path specific to your machine. CI sets nothing and uses the default location, which is correct there.

docs.title: Environments and tasks
docs.text:
environment what it is for dev the day-to-day environment: the package plus the dev tooling, on Python 3.14 py311 … py314 the CI test matrix, one per supported interpreter full dev plus the gis and cloud extras — the only environment where pytest -m gis can run docs MkDocs, mkdocstrings and mike notebook dev plus JupyterLab, for interactive work default the package alone, with no tooling

Run a task with pixi run -e <environment> <task>:

pixi run -e dev main         # the core suite: no pyramids, no GDAL
pixi run -e full test-all    # the whole suite, extras included
pixi run -e dev typecheck    # mypy
pixi run -e dev doctest      # src doctests
pixi run -e dev sample-data  # regenerate the committed LAS/LAZ fixtures
pixi run -e full notebooks   # nbval over docs/examples

pixi task list -e <environment> shows what is available where. The test and tooling tasks live on the dev feature, so they exist in dev, full and the pyXXX environments — not in docs, notebook or default, which have no pytest to run them with.

docs.title: Before you push
docs.text:
pre-commit run --all-files
pixi run -e dev main
pixi run -e dev typecheck

The pre-commit hooks are the same ones CI runs. Two are skipped in CI and should not be skipped locally: no-commit-to-branch (it is a local guard, and CI legitimately runs on main) and mypy (CI runs it in the static job, inside the py314 environment, which is the same feature set as dev).

docs.title: House rules
docs.text:
• The core stays GDAL-free. Only src/pointclouds/convert.py may import pyramids, inside a function, behind a guarded import that names the [gis] extra. tests/test_core_has_no_gdal.py enforces it — keep it green.
  • pointclouds owns point clouds; pyramids owns raster and vector (ADR-0001). Work that belongs upstream is reported there rather than reimplemented here.
  • Conventional Commits, and a branch per change: <type>/<short-description>.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install pointclouds          # core - no GDAL required
pip install pointclouds[gis]     # + pyramids-gis converters
pip install pointclouds[cloud]   # + remote LAZ / COPC
pip install pointclouds[all]

The core installs anywhere numpy runs. The [gis] extra pulls pyramids-gis (and its vendored GDAL) and is only needed for to_dataset() / to_feature_collection().

docs.title: ADR 0001 - point clouds live in their own distribution
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-15

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Point-cloud support (LAS/LAZ/COPC) was evaluated for pyramids (the GIS engine) as an in-repo module behind a [lidar] extra. The surface is expected to grow well past a format reader - classification, segmentation, meshing, level-of-detail, and a PDAL-class pipeline.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Ship point clouds as an independent distribution (pointclouds) that owns the data model and the engine, with pyramids-gis as an optional [gis] extra reached only by the two converter methods. The core depends only on numpy/laspy/pyproj/scipy and is GDAL-free.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The package installs anywhere numpy runs; it does not inherit pyramids' platform matrix for its core.
  • pyramids gains two generic primitives independently (see serapeum-org/pyramids#1135).
  • digitalrivers.lidar migrates here (see serapeum-org/digital-rivers#84, #85).

Full rationale: planning/placement-decision.md.

pointclouds - point cloud (LAS/LAZ/COPC) I/O, filtering, decimation and gridding.

The public entry point is :class:~pointclouds.points.PointCloud. The GIS converters in :mod:pointclouds.convert require the optional [gis] extra; importing the package needs the core dependency set only (numpy / laspy / pyproj / scipy) and never GDAL.

In-memory point cloud: parallel per-dimension arrays plus a CRS.

The constructor builds an eager cloud from arrays already in hand. To read a file, use :meth:read_file, which is header-first and loads records only when they are asked for, or :meth:read_window to pull back only part of a COPC cloud.

class PointCloud:
    """In-memory point cloud: parallel per-dimension arrays plus a CRS.

    The constructor builds an eager cloud from arrays already in hand. To read a file, use
    :meth:`read_file`, which is header-first and loads records only when they are asked for, or
    :meth:`read_window` to pull back only part of a COPC cloud.

    Attributes:
        x: ``(N,)`` float64 x-coordinates.
        y: ``(N,)`` float64 y-coordinates.
        z: ``(N,)`` float64 z-coordinates.
        intensity: ``(N,)`` uint16 return intensity, or empty when the file/caller carried none.
        classification: ``(N,)`` uint8 ASPRS class codes, or empty.
        return_number: ``(N,)`` uint8 return-number-within-pulse, or empty.
        crs: a :class:`pyproj.CRS`, or ``None`` when no SRS is known.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> cloud = PointCloud(x=np.arange(3.0), y=np.zeros(3), z=np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]))
        >>> len(cloud), cloud.count
        (3, 3)
        >>> cloud.to_array(("X", "Z")).shape
        (3, 2)
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        x: np.ndarray,
        y: np.ndarray,
        z: np.ndarray,
        intensity: np.ndarray | None = None,
        classification: np.ndarray | None = None,
        return_number: np.ndarray | None = None,
        crs: CRS | str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Build a cloud from arrays, rejecting coordinate arrays that disagree in length.

        Args:
            x: ``(N,)`` x-coordinates.
            y: ``(N,)`` y-coordinates.
            z: ``(N,)`` z-coordinates.
            intensity: ``(N,)`` return intensity, or ``None`` for an empty array.
            classification: ``(N,)`` ASPRS class codes, or ``None`` for an empty array.
            return_number: ``(N,)`` return numbers, or ``None`` for an empty array.
            crs: anything :class:`pyproj.CRS` accepts, or ``None``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: if ``x``, ``y`` and ``z`` do not all share one length.
        """
        self._x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
        self._y = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64)
        self._z = np.asarray(z, dtype=np.float64)
        self._attributes = {
            "intensity": _as_attribute(intensity, np.uint16),
            "classification": _as_attribute(classification, np.uint8),
            "return_number": _as_attribute(return_number, np.uint8),
        }
        self._crs = CRS.from_user_input(crs) if isinstance(crs, str) else crs
        self._header: _las.LasHeaderInfo | None = None
        self._source: Path | None = None
        self._loaded = True

        n = len(self._x)
        if not (len(self._y) == n and len(self._z) == n):
            raise ValueError(f"x/y/z must share a length; got {len(self._x)}, {len(self._y)}, {len(self._z)}")

    @classmethod
    def read_file(
        cls,
        path: str | Path,
        *,
        lazy: bool | None = None,
        bbox: tuple[float, float, float, float] | None = None,
        resolution: float | None = None,
        level: int | range | None = None,
    ) -> PointCloud:
        """Open a LAS/LAZ file, or a window onto a COPC one.

        Args:
            path: the file to read. A path only - to read a window from an open file object (an ``fsspec``
                handle), call :meth:`read_window` directly; the LAS/LAZ engine behind the non-windowed read
                takes a path.
            lazy: when left unset or ``True`` only the header is read and the record arrays decompress on first
                access; ``False`` reads the records immediately. It has no meaning for a windowed read, where
                the window *is* the read, so passing it together with ``bbox`` / ``resolution`` / ``level`` is
                refused rather than silently ignored.
            bbox: ``(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)`` in the file's CRS. Passing it makes this a windowed read, which
                requires a COPC file - see :meth:`read_window`.
            resolution: target point spacing; makes this a windowed read. Mutually exclusive with ``level``.
            level: an exact octree level or a ``range`` of them; makes this a windowed read. Mutually exclusive
                with ``resolution``.

        Returns:
            A cloud carrying the file's header metadata, and - unless ``lazy`` is ``False`` - its points. With a
            window, whatever :meth:`read_window` returns.

        Raises:
            FileNotFoundError: when the path does not exist.
            ValueError: when the suffix is neither ``.las`` nor ``.laz``; when ``lazy`` is passed together with a
                window argument; or, for a windowed read, anything :meth:`read_window` rejects.

        Examples:
            Without a window the read is header-first: the metadata costs nothing and the records wait:

            >>> cloud = PointCloud.read_file("examples/data/sample.laz")  # doctest: +SKIP
            >>> cloud.count, cloud.crs is not None  # header only - no records touched  # doctest: +SKIP
            (400, True)
            >>> cloud.loaded  # doctest: +SKIP
            False

            Passing a window makes it a COPC read instead, and the cloud comes back already populated:

            >>> window = PointCloud.read_file(  # doctest: +SKIP
            ...     "examples/data/sample.copc.laz", bbox=(155000, 463000, 155020, 463020)
            ... )
            >>> window.count, window.loaded  # doctest: +SKIP
            (121, True)
        """
        if bbox is not None or resolution is not None or level is not None:
            if lazy is not None:
                raise ValueError("lazy has no meaning with a window; a windowed read is always eager")
            return cls.read_window(path, bbox=bbox, resolution=resolution, level=level)
        header = _las.read_header(path)
        cloud = cls.__new__(cls)  # bypass __init__: a lazy cloud has a header but no arrays yet
        cloud._x = _EMPTY_F8
        cloud._y = _EMPTY_F8
        cloud._z = _EMPTY_F8
        cloud._attributes = {name: np.empty(0, dtype=dtype) for name, dtype in _ATTRIBUTE_DTYPES.items()}
        cloud._crs = header.crs
        cloud._header = header
        cloud._source = Path(path)
        cloud._loaded = False
        # lazy is None when unset, which means lazy; only an explicit lazy=False forces an eager load.
        return cloud.load() if lazy is False else cloud

    @classmethod
    def read_window(
        cls,
        source: _copc.Source,
        *,
        bbox: tuple[float, float, float, float] | None = None,
        resolution: float | None = None,
        level: int | range | None = None,
        dimensions: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
    ) -> PointCloud:
        """Read only part of a COPC cloud, using its octree instead of decompressing everything.

        This is the path a large cloud is meant to be read through: ``bbox`` prunes the octree to the chunks
        whose voxels overlap the box, and ``resolution`` stops the descent at the coarsest level that still
        satisfies it. Reading the whole cloud and masking it afterwards costs the full decompression; this does
        not.

        The returned cloud is **eager and header-less**: :attr:`count` and :attr:`bounds` describe the points
        actually read, not the file they came from. Use :func:`pointclouds.io.copc.read_header` for the file's
        own count, bounds and root spacing.

        Args:
            source: the COPC file, as a path or an open file object. A file object is how a remote cloud is
                read - open it with ``fsspec`` (the ``[cloud]`` extra) and pass it in.
            bbox: ``(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)`` in the file's CRS. 2-D: the full z range is kept.
            resolution: target point spacing, in the data's units, measured against the octree's root spacing.
                Mutually exclusive with ``level``.
            level: an exact octree level, or a ``range`` of them. Mutually exclusive with ``resolution``.
            dimensions: which attribute arrays to carry, case-insensitive. ``None`` reads every mapped
                dimension; ``x`` / ``y`` / ``z`` are always read whatever is asked for, since a cloud needs its
                coordinates. See :func:`pointclouds.io.copc.read_window` - this selects what is returned, not
                what laspy decompresses.

        Returns:
            A cloud holding only the selected points, with the file's CRS. A window that selects nothing gives
            an empty cloud, whose :attr:`count` is ``0``.

        Raises:
            FileNotFoundError: when the path does not exist.
            ValueError: when the suffix is not ``.laz``; when the file carries no COPC octree; when ``bbox`` is
                malformed; when ``resolution`` is not positive; or when ``resolution`` and ``level`` are both
                given.

        Examples:
            A box reads a corner of the cloud, and the resulting cloud describes the window it holds:

            >>> window = PointCloud.read_window(  # doctest: +SKIP
            ...     "examples/data/sample.copc.laz", bbox=(155000, 463000, 155020, 463020)
            ... )
            >>> window.count  # 121 of the file's 1600 points  # doctest: +SKIP
            121
            >>> window.bounds  # doctest: +SKIP
            (155000.0, 463000.0, 155020.0, 463020.0)

            A resolution thins the whole extent instead, which is what a zoomed-out view wants:

            >>> coarse = PointCloud.read_window("examples/data/sample.copc.laz", resolution=7.8)  # doctest: +SKIP
            >>> coarse.count, coarse.crs.to_epsg()  # doctest: +SKIP
            (100, 28992)

            A window that selects nothing is an empty cloud, not an error:

            >>> nothing = PointCloud.read_window(  # doctest: +SKIP
            ...     "examples/data/sample.copc.laz", bbox=(0, 0, 1, 1)
            ... )
            >>> nothing.count  # doctest: +SKIP
            0
        """
        # x/y/z are forced into the request: a cloud is built from its coordinates, so a caller asking only for
        # an attribute still needs them. The result is then splatted into the constructor, which is safe because
        # the record contract's keys are exactly the constructor's point parameters (asserted in the tests).
        requested = None if dimensions is None else tuple(dict.fromkeys(("x", "y", "z", *dimensions)))
        crs, arrays = _copc._read_window_with_crs(
            source, bbox=bbox, resolution=resolution, level=level, dimensions=requested
        )
        return cls(crs=crs, **arrays)

    def load(self) -> PointCloud:
        """Read this cloud's record arrays if they are not in memory yet.

        Returns:
            ``self``, so a read can be chained (``PointCloud.read_file(p).load()``).

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: when the cloud has no source file to load from, which cannot happen for a cloud built
                by :meth:`read_file` and always holds for one built from arrays (already loaded).
        """
        if self._loaded:
            return self
        if self._source is None:  # pragma: no cover - unreachable via the public API
            raise RuntimeError("cloud has no source file to load records from")
        arrays = _las.read_points(self._source)
        self._x = arrays["x"]
        self._y = arrays["y"]
        self._z = arrays["z"]
        self._attributes = {name: arrays[name] for name in _ATTRIBUTE_DTYPES}
        self._loaded = True
        return self

    @property
    def loaded(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the record arrays are in memory. Reading this never triggers a load."""
        return self._loaded

    @property
    def source(self) -> Path | None:
        """The file this cloud was read from, or ``None`` when it was built from arrays."""
        return self._source

    @property
    def x(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """``(N,)`` float64 x-coordinates, loading the records first if needed."""
        return self.load()._x

    @property
    def y(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """``(N,)`` float64 y-coordinates, loading the records first if needed."""
        return self.load()._y

    @property
    def z(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """``(N,)`` float64 z-coordinates, loading the records first if needed."""
        return self.load()._z

    @property
    def intensity(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """``(N,)`` uint16 return intensity (empty when absent), loading the records first if needed."""
        return self.load()._attributes["intensity"]

    @property
    def classification(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """``(N,)`` uint8 ASPRS class codes (empty when absent), loading the records first if needed."""
        return self.load()._attributes["classification"]

    @property
    def return_number(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """``(N,)`` uint8 return numbers (empty when absent), loading the records first if needed."""
        return self.load()._attributes["return_number"]

    @property
    def crs(self) -> CRS | None:
        """The cloud's CRS as a :class:`pyproj.CRS`, or ``None``. Answers from the header; never loads records."""
        return self._crs

    @property
    def count(self) -> int:
        """How many points the cloud holds, from the header when there is one.

        This is the cheap question: on a lazy cloud it answers without decompressing a single record, which is
        what ``len(cloud)`` cannot do. The two agree once the records are in memory.
        """
        if self._header is not None:
            return int(self._header.count)
        return int(self._x.shape[0])

    @property
    def bounds(self) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
        """``(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)``, from the header when there is one, else computed from the arrays.

        Raises:
            ValueError: when the cloud is empty and has no header to take bounds from.
        """
        if self._header is not None:
            return self._header.bounds
        if self._x.size == 0:
            raise ValueError("an empty cloud with no header has no bounds")
        return (float(self._x.min()), float(self._y.min()), float(self._x.max()), float(self._y.max()))

    @property
    def dimensions(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """The dimension names available on this cloud.

        For a cloud read from a file this is what the point format declares, straight from the header. For one
        built from arrays it is the coordinates plus whichever attribute arrays are non-empty.
        """
        if self._header is not None:
            return self._header.dimensions
        present = [name for name, values in self._attributes.items() if values.size]
        return ("X", "Y", "Z", *present)

    def to_array(self, dimensions: tuple[str, ...] = ("X", "Y", "Z")) -> np.ndarray:
        """Stack the requested dimensions column-wise into an ``(N, k)`` array.

        Args:
            dimensions: dimension names, case-insensitive (``"X"``/``"Y"``/``"Z"`` map to the coordinate arrays).

        Returns:
            ``(N, k)`` float64 array, one column per requested dimension.

        Raises:
            KeyError: when a requested dimension is not one this container holds.
        """
        self.load()
        lookup = {"x": self._x, "y": self._y, "z": self._z, **self._attributes}
        try:
            cols = [np.asarray(lookup[name.lower()], dtype=float) for name in dimensions]
        except KeyError as exc:
            raise KeyError(f"unknown dimension {exc.args[0]!r}; this cloud holds {sorted(lookup)}") from None
        return np.column_stack(cols)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        """Return how many points are in memory, loading the records first if needed.

        Use :attr:`count` instead when the header's number is enough - that one is free.
        """
        return int(self.load()._x.shape[0])

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Describe the cloud without loading anything."""
        crs = self._crs.to_string() if self._crs is not None else None
        state = "loaded" if self._loaded else "lazy"
        return f"PointCloud(count={self.count}, crs={crs!r}, {state})"

def __init__(
    self,
    x: np.ndarray,
    y: np.ndarray,
    z: np.ndarray,
    intensity: np.ndarray | None = None,
    classification: np.ndarray | None = None,
    return_number: np.ndarray | None = None,
    crs: CRS | str | None = None,

    Args:
        x: ``(N,)`` x-coordinates.

def load(self) -> PointCloud:
    """Read this cloud's record arrays if they are not in memory yet.

    Returns:
        ``self``, so a read can be chained (``PointCloud.read_file(p).load()``).

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: when the cloud has no source file to load from, which cannot happen for a cloud built
            by :meth:`read_file` and always holds for one built from arrays (already loaded).
    """
    if self._loaded:
        return self
    if self._source is None:  # pragma: no cover - unreachable via the public API
        raise RuntimeError("cloud has no source file to load records from")
    arrays = _las.read_points(self._source)
    self._x = arrays["x"]
    self._y = arrays["y"]
    self._z = arrays["z"]
    self._attributes = {name: arrays[name] for name in _ATTRIBUTE_DTYPES}
    self._loaded = True
    return self

            handle), call :meth:`read_window` directly; the LAS/LAZ engine behind the non-windowed read
            takes a path.

        ...     "examples/data/sample.copc.laz", bbox=(155000, 463000, 155020, 463020)
        ... )
        >>> window.count, window.loaded  # doctest: +SKIP

def to_array(self, dimensions: tuple[str, ...] = ("X", "Y", "Z")) -> np.ndarray:
    """Stack the requested dimensions column-wise into an ``(N, k)`` array.

    Args:
        dimensions: dimension names, case-insensitive (``"X"``/``"Y"``/``"Z"`` map to the coordinate arrays).

    Returns:
        ``(N, k)`` float64 array, one column per requested dimension.

    Raises:
        KeyError: when a requested dimension is not one this container holds.
    """
    self.load()
    lookup = {"x": self._x, "y": self._y, "z": self._z, **self._attributes}
    try:
        cols = [np.asarray(lookup[name.lower()], dtype=float) for name in dimensions]
    except KeyError as exc:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown dimension {exc.args[0]!r}; this cloud holds {sorted(lookup)}") from None
    return np.column_stack(cols)

docs.text:
The :class:PointCloud container.

A point cloud is held as parallel 1-D arrays - index i selects the i-th point across every field - so a filter or decimation stays aligned across coordinates and attributes. This module is the nucleus of the package and must import with the core dependency set alone (numpy / laspy / pyproj); it must never import GDAL or pyramids.

Reading is header-first (T-8). :meth:PointCloud.read_file opens a file and, by default, reads only its header: crs, bounds, count and dimensions answer immediately, at a cost independent of the file's size. The record arrays decompress on first access to x / y / z or to any attribute array, or eagerly via :meth:PointCloud.load. The distinction that matters, and the reason count is not an alias for len:

  • cloud.count is the header's point count - free, no records read.
  • len(cloud) is how many points are in memory, so on a lazy cloud it forces the read.

Reading can also be windowed (T-16). :meth:PointCloud.read_window - and read_file(bbox=, resolution=), which delegates to it - asks a COPC file's octree for only the points inside a bounding box, or only a coarse enough level of detail, instead of decompressing the whole cloud and masking it afterwards. A windowed cloud is eager and carries no header, so its count and bounds describe the window rather than the file.

        actually read, not the file they came from. Use :func:`pointclouds.io.copc.read_header` for the file's
        own count, bounds and root spacing.

        Args:
            source: the COPC file, as a path or an open file object. A file object is how a remote cloud is
                read - open it with ``fsspec`` (the ``[cloud]`` extra) and pass it in.
            bbox: ``(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)`` in the file's CRS. 2-D: the full z range is kept.
            resolution: target point spacing, in the data's units, measured against the octree's root spacing.
                Mutually exclusive with ``level``.
            level: an exact octree level, or a ``range`` of them. Mutually exclusive with ``resolution``.
            dimensions: which attribute arrays to carry, case-insensitive. ``None`` reads every mapped
                dimension; ``x`` / ``y`` / ``z`` are always read whatever is asked for, since a cloud needs its
                coordinates. See :func:`pointclouds.io.copc.read_window` - this selects what is returned, not
                what laspy decompresses.

        Returns:
            A cloud holding only the selected points, with the file's CRS. A window that selects nothing gives
            an empty cloud, whose :attr:`count` is ``0``.

        Raises:
            FileNotFoundError: when the path does not exist.
            ValueError: when the suffix is not ``.laz``; when the file carries no COPC octree; when ``bbox`` is
                malformed; when ``resolution`` is not positive; or when ``resolution`` and ``level`` are both
                given.

            A box reads a corner of the cloud, and the resulting cloud describes the window it holds:

            >>> window = PointCloud.read_window(  # doctest: +SKIP
            ...     "examples/data/sample.copc.laz", bbox=(155000, 463000, 155020, 463020)
            ... )
            >>> window.count  # 121 of the file's 1600 points  # doctest: +SKIP
            121
            >>> window.bounds  # doctest: +SKIP
            (155000.0, 463000.0, 155020.0, 463020.0)

            >>> coarse = PointCloud.read_window("examples/data/sample.copc.laz", resolution=7.8)  # doctest: +SKIP
            >>> coarse.count, coarse.crs.to_epsg()  # doctest: +SKIP
            (100, 28992)

            >>> nothing = PointCloud.read_window(  # doctest: +SKIP
            ...     "examples/data/sample.copc.laz", bbox=(0, 0, 1, 1)
            ... )
            >>> nothing.count  # doctest: +SKIP

        # an attribute still needs them. The result is then splatted into the constructor, which is safe because
        # the record contract's keys are exactly the constructor's point parameters (asserted in the tests).

    def load(self) -> PointCloud:

        Returns:
            ``self``, so a read can be chained (``PointCloud.read_file(p).load()``).

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: when the cloud has no source file to load from, which cannot happen for a cloud built
                by :meth:`read_file` and always holds for one built from arrays (already loaded).

            return self

            raise RuntimeError("cloud has no source file to load records from")

        self._x = arrays["x"]
        self._y = arrays["y"]
        self._z = arrays["z"]
        self._attributes = {name: arrays[name] for name in _ATTRIBUTE_DTYPES}
        self._loaded = True
        return self

    def loaded(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the record arrays are in memory. Reading this never triggers a load."""
        return self._loaded

    @property
    def source(self) -> Path | None:
        """The file this cloud was read from, or ``None`` when it was built from arrays."""
        return self._source

    @property
    def x(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """``(N,)`` float64 x-coordinates, loading the records first if needed."""
        return self.load()._x

    @property
    def y(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """``(N,)`` float64 y-coordinates, loading the records first if needed."""
        return self.load()._y

    @property
    def z(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """``(N,)`` float64 z-coordinates, loading the records first if needed."""
        return self.load()._z

    @property
    def intensity(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """``(N,)`` uint16 return intensity (empty when absent), loading the records first if needed."""
        return self.load()._attributes["intensity"]

    @property
    def classification(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """``(N,)`` uint8 ASPRS class codes (empty when absent), loading the records first if needed."""
        return self.load()._attributes["classification"]

    @property
    def return_number(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """``(N,)`` uint8 return numbers (empty when absent), loading the records first if needed."""
        return self.load()._attributes["return_number"]

    @property
    def crs(self) -> CRS | None:
        """The cloud's CRS as a :class:`pyproj.CRS`, or ``None``. Answers from the header; never loads records."""
        return self._crs

    @property
    def count(self) -> int:
        """How many points the cloud holds, from the header when there is one.

        This is the cheap question: on a lazy cloud it answers without decompressing a single record, which is
        what ``len(cloud)`` cannot do. The two agree once the records are in memory.
        """
        if self._header is not None:
            return int(self._header.count)
        return int(self._x.shape[0])

    @property
    def bounds(self) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
        """``(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)``, from the header when there is one, else computed from the arrays.

        Raises:
            ValueError: when the cloud is empty and has no header to take bounds from.
        """
        if self._header is not None:
            return self._header.bounds
        if self._x.size == 0:
            raise ValueError("an empty cloud with no header has no bounds")
        return (float(self._x.min()), float(self._y.min()), float(self._x.max()), float(self._y.max()))

    @property
    def dimensions(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """The dimension names available on this cloud.

        For a cloud read from a file this is what the point format declares, straight from the header. For one
        built from arrays it is the coordinates plus whichever attribute arrays are non-empty.
        """
        if self._header is not None:
            return self._header.dimensions
        present = [name for name, values in self._attributes.items() if values.size]
        return ("X", "Y", "Z", *present)

    def to_array(self, dimensions: tuple[str, ...] = ("X", "Y", "Z")) -> np.ndarray:
        """Stack the requested dimensions column-wise into an ``(N, k)`` array.

        Args:
            dimensions: dimension names, case-insensitive (``"X"``/``"Y"``/``"Z"`` map to the coordinate arrays).

        Returns:
            ``(N, k)`` float64 array, one column per requested dimension.

        Raises:
            KeyError: when a requested dimension is not one this container holds.
        """
        self.load()
        lookup = {"x": self._x, "y": self._y, "z": self._z, **self._attributes}
        try:
            cols = [np.asarray(lookup[name.lower()], dtype=float) for name in dimensions]
        except KeyError as exc:
            raise KeyError(f"unknown dimension {exc.args[0]!r}; this cloud holds {sorted(lookup)}") from None
        return np.column_stack(cols)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        """Return how many points are in memory, loading the records first if needed.

        Use :attr:`count` instead when the header's number is enough - that one is free.
        """
        return int(self.load()._x.shape[0])

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Describe the cloud without loading anything."""
        crs = self._crs.to_string() if self._crs is not None else None
        state = "loaded" if self._loaded else "lazy"
        return f"PointCloud(count={self.count}, crs={crs!r}, {state})"

def __init__(
    self,
    x: np.ndarray,
    y: np.ndarray,
    z: np.ndarray,
    intensity: np.ndarray | None = None,
    classification: np.ndarray | None = None,
    return_number: np.ndarray | None = None,
    crs: CRS | str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Build a cloud from arrays, rejecting coordinate arrays that disagree in length.

    Args:
        x: ``(N,)`` x-coordinates.
        y: ``(N,)`` y-coordinates.
        z: ``(N,)`` z-coordinates.
        intensity: ``(N,)`` return intensity, or ``None`` for an empty array.
        classification: ``(N,)`` ASPRS class codes, or ``None`` for an empty array.
        return_number: ``(N,)`` return numbers, or ``None`` for an empty array.
        crs: anything :class:`pyproj.CRS` accepts, or ``None``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if ``x``, ``y`` and ``z`` do not all share one length.
    """
    self._x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    self._y = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64)
    self._z = np.asarray(z, dtype=np.float64)
    self._attributes = {
        "intensity": _as_attribute(intensity, np.uint16),
        "classification": _as_attribute(classification, np.uint8),
        "return_number": _as_attribute(return_number, np.uint8),
    }
    self._crs = CRS.from_user_input(crs) if isinstance(crs, str) else crs
    self._header: _las.LasHeaderInfo | None = None
    self._source: Path | None = None
    self._loaded = True

    n = len(self._x)
    if not (len(self._y) == n and len(self._z) == n):
        raise ValueError(f"x/y/z must share a length; got {len(self._x)}, {len(self._y)}, {len(self._z)}")

    cls,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    lazy: bool | None = None,
    bbox: tuple[float, float, float, float] | None = None,
    resolution: float | None = None,
    level: int | range | None = None,

    """Open a LAS/LAZ file, or a window onto a COPC one.

    Args:
        path: the file to read. A path only - to read a window from an open file object (an ``fsspec``
            handle), call :meth:`read_window` directly; the LAS/LAZ engine behind the non-windowed read
            takes a path.
        lazy: when left unset or ``True`` only the header is read and the record arrays decompress on first
            access; ``False`` reads the records immediately. It has no meaning for a windowed read, where
            the window *is* the read, so passing it together with ``bbox`` / ``resolution`` / ``level`` is
            refused rather than silently ignored.
        bbox: ``(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)`` in the file's CRS. Passing it makes this a windowed read, which
            requires a COPC file - see :meth:`read_window`.
        resolution: target point spacing; makes this a windowed read. Mutually exclusive with ``level``.
        level: an exact octree level or a ``range`` of them; makes this a windowed read. Mutually exclusive
            with ``resolution``.

    Returns:
        A cloud carrying the file's header metadata, and - unless ``lazy`` is ``False`` - its points. With a
        window, whatever :meth:`read_window` returns.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: when the path does not exist.
        ValueError: when the suffix is neither ``.las`` nor ``.laz``; when ``lazy`` is passed together with a
            window argument; or, for a windowed read, anything :meth:`read_window` rejects.

    Examples:
        Without a window the read is header-first: the metadata costs nothing and the records wait:

        >>> cloud = PointCloud.read_file("examples/data/sample.laz")  # doctest: +SKIP
        >>> cloud.count, cloud.crs is not None  # header only - no records touched  # doctest: +SKIP
        (400, True)
        >>> cloud.loaded  # doctest: +SKIP
        False

        Passing a window makes it a COPC read instead, and the cloud comes back already populated:

        >>> window = PointCloud.read_file(  # doctest: +SKIP
        ...     "examples/data/sample.copc.laz", bbox=(155000, 463000, 155020, 463020)
        ... )
        >>> window.count, window.loaded  # doctest: +SKIP
        (121, True)
    """
    if bbox is not None or resolution is not None or level is not None:
        if lazy is not None:
            raise ValueError("lazy has no meaning with a window; a windowed read is always eager")
        return cls.read_window(path, bbox=bbox, resolution=resolution, level=level)
    header = _las.read_header(path)
    cloud = cls.__new__(cls)  # bypass __init__: a lazy cloud has a header but no arrays yet
    cloud._x = _EMPTY_F8
    cloud._y = _EMPTY_F8
    cloud._z = _EMPTY_F8
    cloud._attributes = {name: np.empty(0, dtype=dtype) for name, dtype in _ATTRIBUTE_DTYPES.items()}
    cloud._crs = header.crs
    cloud._header = header
    cloud._source = Path(path)
    cloud._loaded = False
    # lazy is None when unset, which means lazy; only an explicit lazy=False forces an eager load.
    return cloud.load() if lazy is False else cloud

    # an attribute still needs them. The result is then splatted into the constructor, which is safe because
    # the record contract's keys are exactly the constructor's point parameters (asserted in the tests).
    requested = None if dimensions is None else tuple(dict.fromkeys(("x", "y", "z", *dimensions)))
    crs, arrays = _copc._read_window_with_crs(
        source, bbox=bbox, resolution=resolution, level=level, dimensions=requested
    )
    return cls(crs=crs, **arrays)

def to_array(self, dimensions: tuple[str, ...] = ("X", "Y", "Z")) -> np.ndarray:
    """Stack the requested dimensions column-wise into an ``(N, k)`` array.

    Args:
        dimensions: dimension names, case-insensitive (``"X"``/``"Y"``/``"Z"`` map to the coordinate arrays).

    Returns:
        ``(N, k)`` float64 array, one column per requested dimension.

    Raises:
        KeyError: when a requested dimension is not one this container holds.
    """
    self.load()
    lookup = {"x": self._x, "y": self._y, "z": self._z, **self._attributes}
    try:
        cols = [np.asarray(lookup[name.lower()], dtype=float) for name in dimensions]
    except KeyError as exc:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown dimension {exc.args[0]!r}; this cloud holds {sorted(lookup)}") from None
    return np.column_stack(cols)

docs.title: pointclouds.io.copc
docs.text:
COPC spatially-indexed windowed reads: pull back a bounding box, or a coarser level of detail. (T-16).

A COPC file is a LAZ 1.4 whose chunks are laid out as an octree, with the tree's index stored in the file. That layout is what makes a windowed read possible: given a bounding box, only the chunks whose octree voxels overlap it are fetched and decompressed, and given a target resolution, only the octree levels coarse enough to satisfy it are visited. The alternative - :func:pointclouds.io.las.read_points followed by a mask - reads and decompresses every record first, which is the cost COPC exists to avoid.

Two entry points, mirroring :mod:pointclouds.io.las:

  • :func:read_header answers count / bounds / crs plus the octree's root spacing, touching no point record - the same header-first contract the LAS engine keeps.
  • :func:read_window runs the query and returns record arrays, under the record contract in :mod:pointclouds.io._records, so a window maps onto :class:~pointclouds.points.PointCloud exactly as a full read does.

laspy provides the octree traversal (:class:laspy.CopcReader) and lazrs the per-chunk decompression; both are already core dependencies, so nothing here needs an extra. Everything imports with the core set (numpy, laspy, pyproj) and never touches GDAL.

A COPC source may be a local path or a file object exposing read / seek / tell (the :class:FileObject protocol), which is how a remote cloud is read without this package taking on an HTTP client: open the object with fsspec (the [cloud] extra) and pass it in. The handle must be seekable - COPC is a random-access format - and it stays the caller's to close.

EPT is not implemented here yet. An Entwine tileset is a directory of files behind an ept.json rather than a single indexed file, and laspy has no reader for it, so it needs its own traversal and fetch path - the second half of the issue this module closes the first half of.

def is_copc(source: Source) -> bool:
    """Report whether ``source`` carries a COPC octree.

    This is the cheap question: it reads the header, the VLRs and the octree's root hierarchy page, never a
    point record. On a remote source that is two range requests, not one - the root page sits past the point
    data.

    Args:
        source: the file to inspect, as a path or an open file object.

    Returns:
        ``True`` when the file is a valid COPC, ``False`` when it is a plain LAS/LAZ with no octree.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: when a path does not exist.
        ValueError: when a path's suffix is not ``.laz`` - an uncompressed ``.las`` is never COPC.
        laspy.errors.LazError: when the ``lazrs`` backend is missing. A predicate must not answer ``False`` to a
            question it could not evaluate, so a backend failure surfaces rather than being swallowed.
        laspy.errors.LaspyException: when the file is structurally broken (truncated or corrupt) - distinct from
            "a valid file with no octree", which is the only case that returns ``False``.

    Examples:
        An indexed cloud answers yes, and a plain LAZ answers no rather than raising - that is the question:

        >>> is_copc("examples/data/sample.copc.laz")  # doctest: +SKIP
        True
        >>> is_copc("examples/data/sample.laz")  # doctest: +SKIP
        False

        >>> path = "examples/data/sample.laz"  # doctest: +SKIP
        >>> read_window(path, bbox=(0, 0, 1, 1)) if is_copc(path) else "read it whole instead"  # doctest: +SKIP
        'read it whole instead'
    """
    resolved = _resolve(source)  # a bad suffix or a missing file is an error, not a "no" answer
    try:
        with _reader(resolved):
            return True
    except ValueError:
        return False

The pyramids boundary: importing pyramids happens here and nowhere else.

This is the ONLY module in the package permitted to import pyramids, and it does so lazily inside :func:require_pyramids behind a guarded import. Importing this module with the core dependency set alone must succeed; only calling into the GIS stack requires the [gis] extra.

The converters themselves - to_dataset (grid a cloud to a pyramids Dataset) and to_feature_collection (a decimated cloud to a point FeatureCollection) - land in Phase 2 (plan task T-10), on top of the core ops.grid.to_grid. They are deliberately absent here rather than shipped as raising stubs.

def require_pyramids() -> tuple[Any, Any]:
    """Return ``(Dataset, GeoReference)`` from pyramids, or raise a hint naming the extra.

    Returns:
        The ``pyramids.dataset.Dataset`` and ``GeoReference`` classes.

    Raises:
        ModuleNotFoundError: when pyramids is not installed, with a message that names
            ``pip install pointclouds[gis]`` rather than surfacing the bare import error.
    """
    try:
        from pyramids.dataset import Dataset, GeoReference
    except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - environment-specific
        raise ModuleNotFoundError(_GIS_HINT) from exc
    return Dataset, GeoReference
